title: The haematuria of the long-distance runner
claims: Strenuous exertion has long been known to cause transient urinary abnormalities, including microscopic and less commonly macroscopic haematuria, proteinuria and cylindruria.
Gardner coined the term "athletic pseudonephritis" after finding urinary sediment abnormalities in American football players that disappeared rapidly, usually within 24 hours with rest.
Blacklock described a characteristic cystoscopic appearance with ecchymoses or frank contusions near the interureteric bar, the posterior rim of the internal meatus and the posterior bladder wall.
The proposed mechanism of "10 000 metres haematuria" is repeated impaction of the flaccid posterior bladder wall against the base of the bladder during running.
The first urine voided after a long-distance run often contained frank blood, sometimes with clots, occasionally with suprapubic discomfort or pain at the tip of the penis.
Abnormalities resolve rapidly, usually over 24–48 hours, but recurrent episodes should prompt steps to exclude serious underlying kidney or lower urinary tract disease.
Exercise may unmask underlying disorders such as idiopathic paroxysmal myoglobinuria or march haemoglobinuria.
The editorial concludes that any haematuria, proteinuria or cylindruria should be assumed to be due to underlying urinary tract disease until proved otherwise.

claimVerification.note: 引言：剧烈运动久已知可致短暂血尿、蛋白尿、管型尿。
Gardner 1956：美式橄榄球员尿沉渣异常，休息后多 24 h 内消失，提出 athletic pseudonephritis。
Blacklock：输尿管间嵴、尿道内口后缘后半及膀胱后壁瘀斑/挫伤。
10 000 metres haematuria 机制为膀胱后壁反复撞击膀胱底。
长跑后首次排尿常见鲜红血，可有血块，偶伴耻骨上不适或尿道口痛。
异常多 24–48 h 消退；复发需排除肾或下尿路严重病变。
运动可揭示特发性阵发性肌红蛋白尿或行军性血红蛋白尿。
社论结论：任何血尿/蛋白尿/管型尿在证实前应按尿路疾病处理。
